explanation: All synchronous code runs first: 'start', then main() runs synchronously up to its first await and logs 'async start', then 'end'. Once the synchronous run finishes, the microtask queue drains in registration order: the Promise.resolve().then callback was registered before main() hit await, so it runs first, logging 'promise 1' (and scheduling a second timeout mid-microtask); main()'s continuation after await runs next, logging 'async end'; then the queueMicrotask callback, logging 'microtask 1'. Only after every microtask has drained do the macrotasks (the two setTimeouts) run, in the order they were scheduled: the first timeout (registered synchronously) fires before the second (registered during microtask processing).
